questions.question: 'The silk route was a good example of vibrant pre-modern trade and cultural links between distant parts of the world.' Explain the statement with any two examples.
answer_steps: Trade: Chinese silk and pottery, and textiles and spices from India and Southeast Asia, travelled west, while gold and silver flowed from Europe to Asia.
Culture: early Christian missionaries and later Muslim preachers travelled these routes to Asia, and Buddhism spread from eastern India in several directions along them.

questions.question: 'Sometimes the new crops could make the difference between life and death.' Explain the statement with any two examples.
answer_steps: Europe's poor began to eat better and live longer with the arrival of the humble potato from the Americas.
Ireland's poorest peasants became so dependent on potatoes that when disease destroyed the crop in the mid-1840s, hundreds of thousands died of starvation.

questions.question: Give two examples of different types of global exchanges which took place before the seventeenth century, choosing one example from Asia and one from the Americas.
answer_steps: Asia: the silk routes linked China and India with Europe and northern Africa; Chinese silk, pottery and Indian spices went west, while gold and silver came east; Buddhism spread from eastern India along these routes.
Americas: after Columbus, foods such as potatoes, maize, tomatoes, chillies and groundnuts travelled from America to Europe and Asia.
Also from the Americas: silver from mines in Peru and Mexico enhanced Europe's wealth and financed its trade with Asia.

questions.question: Explain how the global transfer of disease in the pre-modern world helped in the colonisation of the Americas.
answer_steps: The Portuguese and Spanish conquerors carried germs such as smallpox on their persons.
America's original inhabitants had been isolated for millions of years and had no immunity against these diseases, so smallpox spread deep into the continent, even ahead of the Europeans.
It killed and decimated whole communities, weakening resistance and paving the way for conquest; unlike guns, disease could not be bought or captured.

questions.question: Explain how the world shrank and changed in the sixteenth century.
answer_steps: European sailors found a sea route to Asia and crossed the western ocean to America; the Indian subcontinent, central to Indian Ocean trade, became linked to Europe.
America's vast lands, crops and minerals transformed trade; silver from Peru and Mexico enhanced Europe's wealth and financed its trade with Asia.
Smallpox and other germs carried by the Spanish and Portuguese killed America's original inhabitants, who had no immunity, and paved the way for colonisation.
Poverty, hunger, disease and religious persecution in Europe made thousands flee to America, where plantations worked by African slaves grew cotton and sugar for Europe.
As China restricted overseas contacts from the 15th century and the Americas grew in importance, the centre of world trade moved westwards to Europe.

Christian missionaries and later Muslim preachers travelled along them, and Buddhism spread from eastern India in several directions.

questions.question:

*"The Portuguese and Spanish conquest and colonisation of America was decisively under way by the mid-sixteenth century. European conquest was not just a result of superior firepower. In fact, the most powerful weapon of the Spanish conquerors was not a conventional military weapon at all. It was the germs such as those of smallpox that they carried on their person."* (NCERT)

(i) Which two European powers colonised America? (1)

(ii) What was the most powerful weapon of the Spanish conquerors? (1)

(iii) Why did this 'weapon' work so well? (2)
answer_steps: (i) Portugal and Spain.
(ii) Germs such as those of smallpox.

(iii) America's original inhabitants had been isolated for millions of years and had no immunity; smallpox spread deep into the continent, ahead of the Europeans, killing whole communities, and unlike guns it could not be bought or captured.

*"Many of our common foods such as potatoes, soya, groundnuts, maize, tomatoes, chillies, sweet potatoes, and so on were not known to our ancestors until about five centuries ago. These foods were only introduced in Europe and Asia after Christopher Columbus accidentally discovered the vast continent that would later become known as the Americas."* (NCERT)

(i) Name two foods mentioned that came from the Americas. (1)

(ii) Who were the original inhabitants of the Americas from whom these foods came? (1)

(iii) How could a new crop make the difference between life and death? Give one example each way. (2)
answer_steps: (i) Any two: potatoes, soya, groundnuts, maize, tomatoes, chillies, sweet potatoes.
(ii) The American Indians.

(iii) Life: the potato let Europe's poor eat better and live longer. Death: Ireland's poor depended so much on potatoes that when disease destroyed the crop in the mid-1840s, hundreds of thousands starved.
